words.enDefinition: a person who has recently joined an employer

examples.en: The new hire joined us on Monday and spent the morning meeting the team.
examples.zh: 这位「新入职员工」周一加入，上午和团队成员一一见了面。

examples.en: Each new hire receives a copy of the duty roster for the first week.
examples.zh: 每位「新入职员工」都会收到一份第一周的值班表。

collocations: assign a buddy to a new hire

words.enDefinition: the first day someone actually works in a new position

examples.en: On my first day on the job, I helped prepare the returns desk.
examples.zh: 「上班第一天」，我帮忙把退还物品的柜台准备好。

examples.en: My supervisor had a short checklist ready for my first day on the job.
examples.zh: 主管为我「上班第一天」准备了一份简短清单。

collocations: prepare for your first day on the job
on your first day on the job
through your first day on the job

words.enDefinition: a meeting arranged to greet someone joining a workplace or team

examples.en: The welcome meeting gave me a chance to meet people from the other shift.
examples.zh: 「入职欢迎会」让我有机会认识另一个班次的人。

examples.en: I wrote down the team members' names during the welcome meeting last Monday.
examples.zh: 上周一参加「入职欢迎会」时，我记下了团队成员的名字。

words.enDefinition: a colleague assigned to help a new hire settle in and learn workplace routines

examples.en: My onboarding buddy showed me how the team booked study rooms for workshops.
examples.zh: 「入职带教伙伴」教我团队怎么为培训预约自习室。

examples.en: I asked my onboarding buddy which documents I should read before the first shift.
examples.zh: 我问「入职带教伙伴」，上第一班前应该先读哪些文件。

words.enDefinition: the manager directly responsible for supervising a person's day-to-day work

examples.en: My line manager helped me choose which part of the project to start.
examples.zh: 我的「直属经理」帮我决定先做项目的哪一部分。

examples.en: I told my line manager about the timetable clash before the rota was finalized.
examples.zh: 排班表定稿前，我把时间冲突告诉了「直属经理」。

words.enDefinition: a person who coordinates a team's work and guides its members

examples.en: The team lead passed the smaller jobs to those of us working afternoons.
examples.zh: 「团队负责人」把小任务分给我们这些上下午班的人。

examples.en: I checked the priority with the team lead before rearranging my tasks.
examples.zh: 重新安排任务前，我向「团队负责人」核实了优先级。

words.enDefinition: the formal relationship showing whom a worker or team reports to

examples.en: The diagram shows the reporting line from the assistants to the duty manager.
examples.zh: 这张图显示了助理向值班经理汇报的「汇报关系」。

examples.en: I asked how my reporting line would change when I moved to another team.
examples.zh: 我问转到另一个团队后，我的「汇报关系」会怎么变。

collocations: a change in your reporting line

words.enDefinition: a person who reports directly to a particular manager

examples.en: The supervisor met each direct report to discuss plans for the new term.
examples.zh: 主管与每位「直接下属」见面，谈了新学期计划。

examples.en: I learned that a direct report does not go through another manager first.
examples.zh: 我了解到，「直接下属」汇报时无须先经过另一位经理。

words.enDefinition: the hierarchy through which authority and instructions pass in an organization

examples.en: The handbook explained where the shift supervisor sat in the chain of command.
examples.zh: 手册解释了班次主管在「逐级汇报体系」中的位置。

examples.en: I checked the chain of command before forwarding the issue to the department manager.
examples.zh: 把问题转给部门经理前，我查了「逐级汇报体系」。

collocations: go through the chain of command

words.enDefinition: to work under the direct supervision of a specified person

examples.en: I report to the evening supervisor whenever I cover shifts at the main desk.
examples.zh: 我去总服务台代班时，都会「向晚班主管汇报工作」。

examples.en: During the holidays, student assistants report to whichever manager is on duty.
examples.zh: 放假期间，学生助理「向当班的经理汇报工作」。

collocations: report to the head of operations

words.enDefinition: a list of team members with their contact details or roles

examples.en: I used the team directory to find the right person for room bookings.
examples.zh: 我用「团队通讯录」找到了负责房间预约的人。

examples.en: The team directory was updated after two new student workers joined our group.
examples.zh: 两名新的学生员工加入后，「团队通讯录」更新了。

collocations: look someone up in the team directory

words.enDefinition: the part of the day during which staff are expected to be working or available

examples.en: The schedule lists core working hours across the middle of the day.
examples.zh: 排班表把每天中间的一段列为「核心工作时段」。

examples.en: Our team tries to hold shared meetings within the core working hours.
examples.zh: 团队尽量在「核心工作时段」安排大家一起参加的会议。

collocations: be available during core working hours

words.enDefinition: a calendar used to coordinate a group's meetings, shifts or deadlines

examples.en: I added my availability to the team calendar before the new rota was drafted.
examples.zh: 新排班表开始拟定前，我在「团队日历」里填了空闲时间。

examples.en: The team calendar shows who is covering the bookings desk on Friday.
examples.zh: 「团队日历」显示周五由谁顶替预约柜台的班。

collocations: add a meeting to the team calendar

words.enDefinition: a reservation for a shared desk or the process of making it

examples.en: I made a desk booking because my usual seat was taken that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午平时坐的位置有人了，于是我做了「工位预约」。

examples.en: The system sent me a desk booking confirmation with the floor and seat numbers.
examples.zh: 系统发来了「工位预约」确认，上面有楼层和座位号。

words.enDefinition: a workstation used by whichever worker reserves it or finds it available

examples.en: I used a hot desk near the window on the two days I came in.
examples.zh: 我来办公室的两天坐的是窗边的「共享流动工位」。

examples.en: The hot desk has a monitor and a charger that anyone can use.
examples.zh: 「共享流动工位」有显示器和充电器，谁都可以用。

words.enDefinition: the practice of using available shared desks instead of having permanently assigned ones

examples.en: The office switched to hot-desking after several teams began working from home part-time.
examples.zh: 几个团队开始部分时间居家办公后，办公室改成了「不固定工位办公」。

examples.en: During my orientation, the supervisor explained how hot-desking worked on busy days.
examples.zh: 入职介绍时，主管解释了人多的时候怎样「不固定工位办公」。

words.enDefinition: to ask for permission to use a work system or see its records

examples.en: I had to request system access before checking room availability from the desk.
examples.zh: 我得「申请系统访问权限」，才能在柜台查看房间是否空闲。

examples.en: The guide says to request system access through the internal support form.
examples.zh: 指南说，要用内部支持表格「申请系统访问权限」。

collocations: request system access for a new employee

words.enDefinition: a network or online storage space used by several members of a group

examples.en: I saved the updated room list in the shared drive before leaving.
examples.zh: 我离开前，把更新后的房间清单存到了「共享存储盘」。

examples.en: The team keeps booking forms in a separate folder on the shared drive.
examples.zh: 团队把预约表放在「共享存储盘」里的一个单独文件夹里。

collocations: save a file to a shared drive
store documents on a shared drive

words.enDefinition: a shared space in a messaging app for a team to communicate

examples.en: I posted the corrected schedule in the team channel after speaking to my supervisor.
examples.zh: 和主管谈过之后，我把改好的排班表发到了「团队沟通频道」。

examples.en: The team channel is where we post changes that affect all desk staff.
examples.zh: 我们在「团队沟通频道」发布会影响所有柜台员工的变更。

collocations: post an update in the team channel
pin a message in the team channel

words.enDefinition: a board or page used to display announcements for staff

examples.en: The staff noticeboard showed which entrance we should use during the repair work.
examples.zh: 「员工公告栏」标明了维修期间我们该走哪个入口。

examples.en: I put a shift swap request on the staff noticeboard beside the office door.
examples.zh: 我把换班请求贴在办公室门旁的「员工公告栏」上。

collocations: put a message on the staff noticeboard

words.enDefinition: an email inbox monitored by several people who handle messages together

examples.en: I checked the team inbox for replies from students who had booked the workshop.
examples.zh: 我查了「团队共用收件箱」，看看预约培训的学生有没有回复。

examples.en: The manager asked me to reply from the team inbox during my afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 经理让我上下午班时用「团队共用收件箱」回复邮件。

collocations: send a message to the team inbox

words.enDefinition: an invitation giving recipients the details of a planned meeting, often through a calendar

examples.en: The meeting invite included a link to the document we would discuss.
examples.zh: 「会议邀请」里有我们要讨论的文档链接。

examples.en: I accepted the meeting invite once I confirmed that my shift ended before noon.
examples.zh: 确认班次中午前结束后，我接受了「会议邀请」。

words.enDefinition: an overlap or clash between events on someone's schedule

examples.en: I noticed a calendar conflict after my supervisor scheduled the training for Thursday.
examples.zh: 主管把培训安排在周四后，我发现有「日程冲突」。

examples.en: The calendar conflict meant I could attend only the first half of the meeting.
examples.zh: 因为有「日程冲突」，我只能参加会议的前半段。

words.enDefinition: to find out when someone or something is free for use or an event

examples.en: I offered to check availability for everyone before booking the meeting room.
examples.zh: 订会议室之前，我主动帮大家「核实空闲时间」。

examples.en: We had to check availability because some team members worked only on weekends.
examples.zh: 有些成员只在周末上班，所以我们得「核实空闲时间」。

words.enDefinition: to reschedule a meeting for an earlier time or date

examples.en: I asked if we could move a meeting forward to the morning.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「提前开会」，把会议改到上午。

examples.en: We agreed to move a meeting forward by a day before the holiday.
examples.zh: 我们同意在假期前「提前开会」，把会议往前挪一天。

collocations: move a meeting forward by an hour
ask to move a meeting forward
move a meeting forward to Monday

words.enDefinition: to move a scheduled meeting to a later time or date

examples.en: Could we push back a meeting booked for noon until after the workshop ends?
examples.zh: 能不能「把会议推迟」，原定中午开的这场会等培训结束后再开？

examples.en: I asked whether we could push back a meeting until the afternoon shift began.
examples.zh: 我问能不能「把会议推迟」，等下午班开始再开。

collocations: push back a meeting by thirty minutes
ask to push back a meeting
push back a meeting until Friday

words.enDefinition: to reserve a period of time for a particular task or activity

examples.en: I decided to block off time on Friday to prepare for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我决定周五「在日程上预留时间」准备培训。

examples.en: The supervisor asked us to block off time for the new starter's orientation.
examples.zh: 主管让我们「在日程上预留时间」，参加新同事的入职介绍。

collocations: block off time for a meeting
block off time on your calendar

words.enDefinition: a brief team meeting typically used to share progress and identify obstacles

examples.en: At the stand-up meeting, each person shared what they planned to finish that day.
examples.zh: 「简短进度会」上，每个人说了当天准备完成什么。

examples.en: I mentioned the missing booking records at our regular stand-up meeting on Monday.
examples.zh: 我在周一例行「简短进度会」上提到了缺失的预约记录。

words.enDefinition: a brief informal gathering to exchange information or coordinate immediate work

examples.en: We held a team huddle before opening the reception desk to visitors.
examples.zh: 接待台对访客开放前，我们开了个「团队短碰头会」。

examples.en: The supervisor used the team huddle to share the plan for a busy afternoon.
examples.zh: 主管在「团队短碰头会」上介绍了下午繁忙时段的安排。

words.enDefinition: a meeting with a manager above someone's direct supervisor

examples.en: The skip-level meeting gave our team time to ask the department manager questions.
examples.zh: 「跨级沟通会」给了团队向部门经理提问的时间。

examples.en: I prepared one question about training before attending my first skip-level meeting.
examples.zh: 第一次参加「跨级沟通会」之前，我准备了一个有关培训的问题。

words.enDefinition: the first formal meeting to introduce a project, its goals and responsibilities

examples.en: The kickoff meeting clarified who would look after the workshop bookings that term.
examples.zh: 「项目启动会」明确了那个学期由谁负责培训预约。

examples.en: I shared a short timetable at the kickoff meeting for the exhibition project.
examples.zh: 展览项目的「项目启动会」上，我分享了一份简短的进度表。

words.enDefinition: a topic included regularly on the agenda for a series of meetings

examples.en: The room booking update became a standing agenda item during the exam period.
examples.zh: 考试期间，房间预约的最新情况成了「固定议程事项」。

examples.en: The chair made the equipment check a standing agenda item for our weekly meeting.
examples.zh: 主持人把设备检查列为周会的「固定议程事项」。

collocations: a standing agenda item on safety

words.enDefinition: the person responsible for recording the main discussion and decisions in a meeting

examples.en: Our minute taker checked how to spell the names before writing the notes.
examples.zh: 「会议记录员」在记笔记前先核对了姓名怎么拼。

examples.en: The minute taker asked the chair to repeat the final decision slowly.
examples.zh: 「会议记录员」请主持人慢一点再说一遍最终决定。

words.enDefinition: to write an official record of the main points and decisions in a meeting

examples.en: The coordinator asked me to take minutes because our usual note taker was away.
examples.zh: 平时做记录的人不在，协调员让我「做会议纪要」。

examples.en: I learned to take minutes without trying to write down every word spoken.
examples.zh: 我学会了「做会议纪要」，不必在会上一字不漏地记。

words.enDefinition: the person accountable for following up and completing an agreed action

examples.en: The notes named an action owner for every task agreed at the meeting.
examples.zh: 纪要为会上确定的每项任务列出了一位「待办事项负责人」。

examples.en: I checked with the action owner before changing the date on the team board.
examples.zh: 改团队看板上的日期前，我先问了「待办事项负责人」。

words.enDefinition: an ongoing record of decisions, often including decisions' dates and reasons

examples.en: I added the revised schedule to the decision log after the team approved it.
examples.zh: 团队批准调整后的排班后，我把它记进了「决策记录表」。

examples.en: The decision log explained why the team chose a smaller room that week.
examples.zh: 「决策记录表」解释了团队那周为什么选了较小的房间。

collocations: record a choice in the decision log

words.enDefinition: a topic set aside during a meeting so it can be addressed later

examples.en: The chair noted the equipment request as a parking lot item for next week.
examples.zh: 主持人把设备申请列为「暂缓讨论的议题」，留到下周。

examples.en: We returned to the parking lot item when the urgent decisions were finished.
examples.zh: 紧急决定都做完后，我们回头讨论了那个「暂缓讨论的议题」。

collocations: return to a parking lot item

words.enDefinition: a particular matter listed or raised for a group to talk about

examples.en: I added one discussion point about the new opening hours to the meeting notes.
examples.zh: 我在会议记录里增加了一项关于新营业时间的「待讨论的事项」。

examples.en: The main discussion point was whether two people were needed at the desk.
examples.zh: 主要「待讨论的事项」是柜台是否需要安排两个人。

words.enDefinition: work or communication after a meeting to confirm decisions and carry out next steps

examples.en: I sent a meeting follow-up with the links and the two agreed dates.
examples.zh: 我发了封「会后跟进」邮件，里面有链接和两个商定日期。

examples.en: The meeting follow-up reminded us who would contact the students on the waiting list.
examples.zh: 「会后跟进」提醒了我们由谁联系候补名单上的学生。

words.enDefinition: to send a meeting's written record to the people who need it

examples.en: The chair asked me to circulate the minutes once she had checked them.
examples.zh: 主持人请我等她核对完再「分发会议纪要」。

examples.en: I waited until Friday to circulate the minutes because two names needed correcting.
examples.zh: 有两个人的名字要改，所以我等到周五才「分发会议纪要」。

words.enDefinition: to make sure someone continues to receive relevant information and updates

examples.en: Please keep me in the loop if the room changes before tomorrow's workshop.
examples.zh: 如果明天培训前换了场地，请「让我随时知道进展」。

examples.en: I'll keep you in the loop while the supervisor checks the new schedule.
examples.zh: 主管核对新排班时，我会「让你随时知道进展」。

collocations: keep someone in the loop about changes
promise to keep someone in the loop
make sure to keep someone in the loop

words.enDefinition: used to pass along information without necessarily requesting any action

examples.en: I forwarded the change for your information and kept the original email attached.
examples.zh: 我把变更转发「供你了解」，并保留了原邮件。

examples.en: The coordinator marked the update for your information because no reply was needed.
examples.zh: 协调员在更新上标注「供你了解」，因为无须回复。

words.enDefinition: provided so that someone can check or consult the information later

examples.en: I attached last week's timetable for reference when proposing the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 我提议延长开放时间时，附了上周的时间表「供参考」。

examples.en: The supervisor kept a copy for reference after removing the old notice.
examples.zh: 主管撤下旧通知后保留了一份副本「供参考」。

words.enDefinition: used to refer back to points agreed or mentioned in an earlier conversation

examples.en: I opened the email with “As discussed” and listed the two agreed dates.
examples.zh: 我在邮件开头写「正如之前谈过的」，接着列出商定的两个日期。

examples.en: As discussed, the bookings desk will stay open until seven on Friday.
examples.zh: 「正如之前谈过的」，预约柜台周五会营业到七点。

words.enDefinition: a brief advance notice about something that another person should know

examples.en: I sent a quick heads-up about the printer before the evening shift started.
examples.zh: 晚班开始之前，我发消息「简单提前告知」了一下打印机的情况。

examples.en: The coordinator gave us a quick heads-up about roadworks near the main entrance.
examples.zh: 协调员「简单提前告知」我们，主入口附近正在修路。

collocations: a quick heads-up about a change

words.enDefinition: a short report on what has been done and what is still underway

examples.en: I sent a progress update after finishing the first set of timetable changes.
examples.zh: 做完第一批时间表调整后，我发了条「进展更新」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked for a progress update before approving the next round of work.
examples.zh: 主管想先看一下「进展更新」，再批准下一轮工作。

words.enDefinition: a structured account of what a project or task is doing at a particular time

examples.en: My status report covered completed bookings, missing forms and the next deadline.
examples.zh: 我的「状态报告」写了已完成的预约、缺的表格和下一个截止日期。

examples.en: The team added a note about equipment delays to the weekly status report.
examples.zh: 团队在每周的「状态报告」里加了一条设备延误说明。

words.enDefinition: to tell the relevant person what issue is preventing work from moving forward

examples.en: I used the team channel to report a blocker with the room booking form.
examples.zh: 我在团队频道「报告了阻碍进度的问题」，说明预约表出了什么问题。

examples.en: The supervisor asked us to report a blocker before changing any agreed deadlines.
examples.zh: 主管要求我们先「报告阻碍进度的问题」，再改商定的截止时间。

collocations: report a blocker to your manager
use the task board to report a blocker

words.enDefinition: a choice expected to be made but not yet settled

examples.en: The pending decision about opening hours was mentioned in the shift notes.
examples.zh: 交班记录提到了关于开放时间「尚待作出的决定」。

examples.en: I asked who was responsible for the pending decision before booking the room.
examples.zh: 预订房间前，我问谁负责那项「尚待作出的决定」。

collocations: a pending decision on the schedule

words.enDefinition: the person with responsibility for making or approving a particular decision

examples.en: We named a decision owner for questions about the layout of the reception desk.
examples.zh: 我们为接待柜台布局相关问题指定了一位「决策负责人」。

examples.en: The decision owner listened to the students before agreeing to the timetable change.
examples.zh: 「决策负责人」在同意调整时间表前，先听取了学生的意见。

words.enDefinition: a task that has been assigned or planned but still needs to be done

examples.en: The supervisor gave me one outstanding task to complete before the office closed.
examples.zh: 办公室关门前，主管交给我一项「未完成的任务」。

examples.en: I moved each outstanding task onto the new list before leaving for the weekend.
examples.zh: 周末离开前，我把每项「未完成的任务」移进了新清单。

words.enDefinition: the issue or task considered most important at the present time

examples.en: The current priority is checking the bookings for next week's exhibition at the library.
examples.zh: 「当前优先事项」是核对下周图书馆展览的预约。

examples.en: I confirmed the current priority with my supervisor before starting the long spreadsheet.
examples.zh: 开始制作那份很长的电子表格前，我和主管确认了「当前优先事项」。

words.enDefinition: a task listed for future work that has not yet been scheduled or completed

examples.en: The broken printer was added as a backlog item after the temporary repair.
examples.zh: 打印机临时修好后，后续维修被列为「积压待办项」。

examples.en: I checked whether the backlog item had been assigned to anyone that week.
examples.zh: 我查了一下，那周有没有人领到这项「积压待办项」。

words.enDefinition: to accept responsibility for completing a task and dealing with issues along the way

examples.en: The supervisor asked me to take ownership of a task that needed two approvals.
examples.zh: 主管让我「主动负责一项任务」，这项任务需要两次审批。

examples.en: I offered to take ownership of a task relating to the workshop's attendance records.
examples.zh: 我主动提出「负责一项任务」，处理培训的出勤记录。

collocations: take ownership of a task from start to finish
be willing to take ownership of a task
ask someone to take ownership of a task

words.enDefinition: to begin working on a task available for someone to take

examples.en: I offered to pick up a task that was left after the morning meeting.
examples.zh: 上午开完会还有一个任务没人接，我主动提出「接手一项任务」。

examples.en: At the start of the shift, each volunteer can pick up a task.
examples.zh: 每个志愿者上班时都可以「接手一项任务」。

collocations: offer to pick up a task
pick up a task from the list
available to pick up a task

words.enDefinition: to transfer responsibility for a piece of work to another person

examples.en: I needed to hand over a task before leaving for my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 去上下午的课之前，我需要「把任务交接出去」。

examples.en: The team used shared notes whenever someone had to hand over a task.
examples.zh: 每当有人要「把任务交接出去」，团队就会使用共享记录。

collocations: hand over a task to a colleague
prepare to hand over a task
hand over a task before leaving

words.enDefinition: to give another person authority and responsibility for a particular part of work

examples.en: Our supervisor decided to delegate responsibility for the late bookings to one person.
examples.zh: 主管决定「委派职责」，由一个人负责处理晚间的预约。

examples.en: The guide explains when a student team lead can delegate responsibility to others.
examples.zh: 指南解释了学生团队负责人什么时候可以把「职责委派」给别人。

words.enDefinition: written information passed to the person taking over a job or task

examples.en: I left handover notes about the missing keys for the evening desk staff.
examples.zh: 我在「交接记录」里写了钥匙缺失的事，给晚班柜台人员看。

examples.en: The handover notes explained which bookings still needed confirmation after I went home.
examples.zh: 「交接记录」说明了我回家后还有哪些预约需要确认。

words.enDefinition: the transfer of responsibility and information from one work shift to the next

examples.en: We mentioned the room change during shift handover so the next team knew.
examples.zh: 我们在「班次交接」时提了换房间的事，让下一班团队知情。

examples.en: The shift handover usually takes place at the reception desk just before lunch.
examples.zh: 「班次交接」通常在午饭前不久于接待台进行。

collocations: report an issue during shift handover

words.enDefinition: to work a scheduled shift in place of someone who cannot attend

examples.en: I offered to cover a shift after my class moved to another day.
examples.zh: 我的课改到另一天后，我主动提出「顶替一个班次」。

examples.en: The manager asked if I could cover a shift during the exam break.
examples.zh: 经理问我能不能在考试间歇「顶替一个班次」。

collocations: ask someone to cover a shift
be available to cover a shift

words.enDefinition: to exchange scheduled work periods with another person

examples.en: We agreed to swap shifts so I could attend the afternoon lab session.
examples.zh: 我们同意「互相换班」，让我能参加下午的实验课。

examples.en: I asked if we could swap shifts before the rota was finalized.
examples.zh: 排班表定下来前，我问能不能「互相换班」。

words.enDefinition: to ask a manager or employer for a period away from work

examples.en: I used the staff portal to request time off before my final project presentation.
examples.zh: 毕业项目展示之前，我在员工平台上「申请休假」。

examples.en: The handbook says to request time off through the supervisor who prepares the schedule.
examples.zh: 手册说要通过负责排班的主管「申请休假」。

collocations: request time off through the portal
request time off for an appointment

words.enDefinition: a notice telling the relevant people that someone will be absent from work

examples.en: I sent an absence notification to the person who managed the reception rota.
examples.zh: 我给管理接待台排班的人发了「缺勤通知」。

examples.en: The instructions said the absence notification should include the shift I would miss.
examples.zh: 说明说，「缺勤通知」应写明我会缺哪个班次。

words.enDefinition: to tell your workplace that you are ill and cannot come in to work

examples.en: I had to call in sick before the library desk opened on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一图书馆柜台开门前，我得「打电话请病假」。

examples.en: The handbook lists the number to use if you need to call in sick.
examples.zh: 手册列出了需要「打电话请病假」时该拨的号码。

collocations: call in sick for a shift
call in sick at short notice

words.enDefinition: a meeting to discuss an employee's return after a period away from work

examples.en: My supervisor arranged a return-to-work meeting after I came back from sick leave.
examples.zh: 病假结束后，主管安排了一次「复工沟通会」。

examples.en: At the return-to-work meeting, we discussed which duties I could start with.
examples.zh: 「复工沟通会」上，我们谈了我可以先做哪些工作。

words.enDefinition: the assignment of enough team members to keep work or a service running

examples.en: I checked team coverage before asking whether I could leave an hour earlier.
examples.zh: 我先看了「团队值守安排」，再问自己能不能提前一小时走。

examples.en: The supervisor adjusted team coverage after a student worker cancelled their evening shift.
examples.zh: 一名学生员工取消晚班后，主管调整了「团队值守安排」。

words.enDefinition: a calendar showing when staff members are scheduled to be away from work

examples.en: The leave calendar showed that two desk workers would be away on Friday.
examples.zh: 「员工休假日历」显示，周五有两名柜台员工休假。

examples.en: I checked the leave calendar before asking for the same afternoon off.
examples.zh: 我先查了「员工休假日历」，再申请那个下午休假。

collocations: add a date to the leave calendar

words.enDefinition: the distribution of work so that no person or group carries too much

examples.en: We reviewed workload balance after one person received three large bookings to process.
examples.zh: 有人接连分到三个大预约后，我们检查了「工作量分配平衡」。

examples.en: My supervisor changed the rota to improve workload balance across the desk team.
examples.zh: 主管调整了排班，让柜台团队的「工作量分配更加平衡」。

words.enDefinition: estimating available time or resources and deciding how to use them for expected work

examples.en: The team used capacity planning to prepare for longer opening hours during exams.
examples.zh: 团队通过「人力与工作量规划」为考试期间延长开放时间做准备。

examples.en: During capacity planning, we checked whether everyone could work their usual shifts.
examples.zh: 进行「人力与工作量规划」时，我们核实每个人能不能上平时的班。

collocations: use capacity planning for busy periods

words.enDefinition: an approximate schedule that can be refined when more details are known

examples.en: I brought a rough timeline to the meeting so the team could suggest dates.
examples.zh: 我带去一份「大致时间安排」，让团队在会上提出建议日期。

examples.en: The rough timeline left two weeks for checking the exhibition materials before printing.
examples.zh: 「大致时间安排」在印刷前留了两周核对展览材料。

words.enDefinition: a schedule showing when a project or its completed parts will be delivered

examples.en: The delivery timeline shows when each poster must reach the campus print shop.
examples.zh: 「交付时间安排」标明了每张海报必须何时送到校内印刷店。

examples.en: I updated the delivery timeline after the workshop moved to a later date.
examples.zh: 培训延期后，我调整了「交付时间安排」。

words.enDefinition: to complete and provide the agreed work by the planned date

examples.en: We used a smaller print run so the supplier could deliver on time.
examples.zh: 我们减少了印量，让供应商能够「准时交付」。

examples.en: I told the supervisor what help I needed to deliver on time.
examples.zh: 我告诉主管，要「准时交付」需要得到哪些帮助。

collocations: be able to deliver on time
work together to deliver on time
make sure to deliver on time

words.enDefinition: a person or team designated to receive issues that cannot be handled at the current level

examples.en: The duty manager was the escalation point for issues beyond the desk team's authority.
examples.zh: 超出柜台团队权限的问题，由值班经理担任「问题升级对接人」。

examples.en: I checked the schedule to see who was our escalation point that afternoon.
examples.zh: 我查了排班表，看看那天下午的「问题升级对接人」是谁。

words.enDefinition: the route an issue follows to reach people with higher authority or relevant expertise

examples.en: The guide shows the escalation path for complaints the reception team cannot resolve.
examples.zh: 指南写明了接待团队解决不了投诉时的「逐级上报路径」。

examples.en: We agreed on an escalation path before opening the temporary help desk.
examples.zh: 临时服务台开放前，我们定下了一条「逐级上报路径」。

collocations: an escalation path for urgent issues

words.enDefinition: to tell others about something before it happens, so they have time to prepare

examples.en: I tried to give advance notice before moving my shift to another day.
examples.zh: 我想把班次改到另一天，尽量先「提前通知」大家。

examples.en: The coordinator asked us to give advance notice of equipment needed for a workshop.
examples.zh: 协调员请我们「提前通知」培训需要用哪些设备。

collocations: give advance notice of a change
give advance notice to your supervisor
be able to give advance notice

words.enDefinition: to give a group the essential information they need before acting

examples.en: The supervisor stopped to brief the team before the doors opened to visitors.
examples.zh: 大门对访客开放前，主管停下来「向团队做简要说明」。

examples.en: I used the first minute to brief the team on the room change.
examples.zh: 我用第一分钟「向团队做简要说明」，告诉大家场地变更了。

collocations: brief the team on a change
brief the team before a shift
ask someone to brief the team

words.enDefinition: to give someone enough current information to understand a situation and take part

examples.en: Could you bring me up to speed on the new rota before lunch?
examples.zh: 午饭前你能让我「了解一下新排班的最新情况」吗？

examples.en: I can bring you up to speed on the bookings before the desk opens.
examples.zh: 柜台开门前，我可以「让你了解预约的最新情况」。

collocations: bring someone up to speed on changes
quickly bring someone up to speed
offer to bring someone up to speed

words.enDefinition: to learn enough about a job or situation to work effectively at the current stage

examples.en: I spent my first morning reading the project notes to get up to speed.
examples.zh: 第一天上午，我读了项目记录，想尽快「弄清情况跟上进度」。

examples.en: The supervisor gave me time to get up to speed before answering calls.
examples.zh: 主管让我先「弄清情况跟上进度」，再开始接电话。

collocations: get up to speed on a project
help someone get up to speed

words.enDefinition: a meeting for transferring information and responsibilities to people taking over

examples.en: I brought the incomplete bookings list to the handover meeting on my final day.
examples.zh: 最后一天，我带着未办完的预约清单参加了「交接会」。

examples.en: The handover meeting covered the upcoming workshop and the room key arrangements.
examples.zh: 「交接会」谈了即将举行的培训以及房间钥匙怎么交接。

words.enDefinition: to make clear what people should expect from one another or from a task

examples.en: We used the kickoff meeting to set expectations about how often we would report progress.
examples.zh: 我们用启动会「明确预期要求」，约定多久汇报一次进度。

examples.en: I asked the supervisor to set expectations for how quickly we should reply.
examples.zh: 我请主管「明确预期要求」，告诉我们应该多久内回复。

words.enDefinition: to agree which tasks or goals should receive attention first

examples.en: We took five minutes to align on priorities before starting the afternoon shift.
examples.zh: 下午班开始前，我们花了五分钟「就优先事项达成一致」。

examples.en: The manager asked both teams to align on priorities for the busy week.
examples.zh: 经理让两个团队「就优先事项达成一致」，准备度过繁忙的一周。

collocations: align on priorities for the week

words.enDefinition: to decide together what actions should be taken after a discussion or event

examples.en: We stayed a few minutes after the meeting to agree on next steps.
examples.zh: 开完会我们多留了几分钟，来「商定接下来怎么做」。

examples.en: I asked whether we could agree on next steps before sending the summary.
examples.zh: 我问能不能在发送摘要之前先「商定接下来怎么做」。

collocations: meet to agree on next steps
agree on next steps with the team
agree on next steps before leaving

words.enDefinition: to put a decision into a written or electronic record for later reference

examples.en: I asked the minute taker to record a decision about the updated schedule.
examples.zh: 我请会议记录员「记录一项决定」，是关于更新排班表的。

examples.en: The template has a separate line to record a decision after each discussion.
examples.zh: 模板留了一行，供每项讨论结束后「记录一项决定」。

collocations: record a decision in the minutes
make sure to record a decision

words.enDefinition: to consider a previous decision again, often after circumstances or information change

examples.en: We agreed to revisit a decision after checking how many students actually registered.
examples.zh: 我们同意查清实际注册人数之后，再「重新讨论一项决定」。

examples.en: The new figures led the team to revisit a decision about desk coverage.
examples.zh: 有了新数据，团队决定「重新讨论一项决定」，也就是柜台怎么排人。

collocations: revisit a decision with new information
revisit a decision at the next meeting

words.enDefinition: to give specific comments that help someone understand what works and what to improve

examples.en: The supervisor showed us how to give constructive feedback after the practice session.
examples.zh: 练习结束后，主管示范了怎样「给出建设性反馈」。

examples.en: I tried to give constructive feedback by pointing to one moment in the recording.
examples.zh: 我试着「给出建设性反馈」，具体指出录像中的一个片段。

collocations: give constructive feedback to a colleague
give constructive feedback on a draft

words.enDefinition: a planned conversation to discuss what worked well and what could improve

examples.en: The feedback session gave me a chance to ask about my first week.
examples.zh: 「反馈交流会」让我有机会询问自己第一周的表现。

examples.en: I brought two examples of my work to the feedback session on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二参加「反馈交流会」时，我带了两份工作样例。

words.enDefinition: a brief meeting to review someone's recent work and discuss any needed support

examples.en: My performance check-in focused on how confidently I handled difficult requests at the desk.
examples.zh: 我的「工作表现简谈」主要聊了我处理柜台棘手请求时发挥得怎么样。

examples.en: The manager moved my performance check-in to the first week of the new term.
examples.zh: 经理把「工作表现简谈」改到了新学期第一周。

words.enDefinition: a discussion about a worker's skills, learning and possible future responsibilities

examples.en: The development conversation helped me choose one skill to practise during my placement.
examples.zh: 「职业发展交流」帮我选定了一项在实习中要练习的技能。

examples.en: I asked about training options during my development conversation with the library manager.
examples.zh: 与图书馆经理做「职业发展交流」时，我问了有哪些培训可以选。

collocations: a development conversation with your manager

words.enDefinition: a plan setting goals and activities for improving a person's work-related skills

examples.en: I added a spreadsheet course to my professional development plan after the review.
examples.zh: 评估后，我把一门电子表格课程加进了「职业发展计划」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked me to share my professional development plan before the next meeting.
examples.zh: 主管让我在下次开会前分享「职业发展计划」。

words.enDefinition: an activity or experience that helps a person build skills for future work

examples.en: My manager described the extra training as a development opportunity for student staff.
examples.zh: 经理说，额外培训是学生员工获得的「发展能力的机会」。

examples.en: I used the workshop as a development opportunity to practise answering common questions.
examples.zh: 我把培训当作「发展能力的机会」，借此练习怎样回答常见问题。

words.enDefinition: training people to perform different roles so they can cover one another's work

examples.en: Our cross-training included time at the returns desk and the main reception point.
examples.zh: 我们的「跨岗位培训」包括在退还物品柜台和总接待处工作一段时间。

examples.en: The manager used cross-training to make sure someone could cover the early shift.
examples.zh: 经理通过「跨岗位培训」确保有人能顶早班。

words.enDefinition: a message or form asking someone to comment on a piece of work or performance

examples.en: I sent a feedback request with one question about the revised room guide.
examples.zh: 我发了一条「反馈请求」，询问新版场地指南的一个细节。

examples.en: The feedback request asked the reviewer to focus on the opening section.
examples.zh: 「反馈请求」请审阅人把重点放在开头。

collocations: attach a draft to a feedback request

words.enDefinition: public or private appreciation from people who work alongside someone

examples.en: The team channel has a space for peer recognition after a busy shift.
examples.zh: 团队频道里有地方可以在忙完一个班次后表达「同事间的认可」。

examples.en: The supervisor encouraged peer recognition when someone helped outside their usual role.
examples.zh: 有人主动帮忙做本职之外的工作时，主管鼓励大家表达「同事间的认可」。

words.enDefinition: to acknowledge the contribution a colleague made to a result

examples.en: I wanted to give credit to a colleague who had checked every booking.
examples.zh: 我想「肯定一位同事的贡献」，因为对方核对了每一笔预约。

examples.en: The manager asked me to give credit to a colleague when sharing our results.
examples.zh: 经理让我在分享团队成果时「肯定一位同事的贡献」。

collocations: give credit to a colleague for helping
remember to give credit to a colleague
give credit to a colleague in public

words.enDefinition: a meeting where a team reviews a recent period of work and plans improvements

examples.en: Our team retrospective focused on why visitors had queued at the wrong entrance.
examples.zh: 「团队复盘会」主要讨论访客为什么会在错误的入口排队。

examples.en: I wrote down one practical change during the team retrospective after the workshop.
examples.zh: 培训后的「团队复盘会」上，我记下了一项可实行的改进。

collocations: take part in a team retrospective

words.enDefinition: a question or heading used to identify successful parts of an activity

examples.en: The manager asked what went well during our first week at the temporary desk.
examples.zh: 经理问我们临时柜台第一周「哪些地方做得好」。

examples.en: I listed what went well before suggesting any changes to the handover.
examples.zh: 我先列出「哪些地方做得好」，再提出交接方面的改动。

words.enDefinition: parts of someone's work or a process that could be made better

examples.en: The feedback note listed two areas for improvement in my handling of enquiries.
examples.zh: 反馈记录列了我处理咨询时两个「可以改进的方面」。

examples.en: We picked one of the areas for improvement to discuss at our next meeting.
examples.zh: 我们选了一项「可以改进的方面」，准备在下次开会时讨论。

collocations: focus on specific areas for improvement

words.enDefinition: to contact your manager briefly to share an update, ask something or confirm a plan

examples.en: You can check in with your manager before changing the reception schedule.
examples.zh: 调整接待排班前，你可以先「找主管简短沟通」。

examples.en: The handbook says to check in with your manager at the start of training.
examples.zh: 手册说，培训开始时应该「找主管简短沟通」。

collocations: check in with your manager regularly
check in with your manager about a change
remember to check in with your manager

words.enDefinition: usual expectations for appropriate and considerate conduct at work

examples.en: The induction covered workplace etiquette for staff using the shared kitchen and meeting rooms.
examples.zh: 入职介绍讲了员工使用共用厨房和会议室时的「职场礼仪」。

examples.en: I asked a colleague about workplace etiquette before bringing food into the training room.
examples.zh: 带食物进培训室前，我先问了同事相关的「职场礼仪」。

words.enDefinition: a Friday when a workplace allows clothes more casual than its usual standards

examples.en: I asked whether dress-down Friday applied to staff working at the main reception desk.
examples.zh: 我问在总接待台上班的人可不可以参加「周五便装日」。

examples.en: The notice about dress-down Friday listed the areas where uniforms were still needed.
examples.zh: 「周五便装日」的通知列出了仍需穿制服的区域。

words.enDefinition: a team whose members work in a mixture of on-site and remote settings

examples.en: Our hybrid team used shared notes so people at home could follow the meeting.
examples.zh: 我们是「混合办公团队」，用共享记录让在家办公的人也能了解会议情况。

examples.en: The hybrid team met in person once a month during the placement.
examples.zh: 实习期间，「混合办公团队」每月线下见一次面。

words.enDefinition: a coworker who usually works from another location instead of a shared office

examples.en: I sent the photographs to a remote colleague before the exhibition opened.
examples.zh: 展览开幕前，我把照片发给了一位「远程办公的同事」。

examples.en: A remote colleague joined the discussion by video while we used the meeting room.
examples.zh: 我们在会议室讨论，一位「远程办公的同事」通过视频加入。

collocations: share files with a remote colleague

words.enDefinition: a document defining a team's shared purpose, roles and agreed ways of working

examples.en: The team charter explains who can approve changes to the workshop schedule.
examples.zh: 「团队协作章程」写明了谁可以批准修改培训安排。

examples.en: We updated the team charter after a new group of students joined.
examples.zh: 一批新同学加入后，我们更新了「团队协作章程」。

words.enDefinition: shared expectations for how people behave and work together on a team

examples.en: One of our team norms is to post schedule changes where everyone can see them.
examples.zh: 把改期信息发到大家都能看到的地方，是我们的「团队共同遵守的习惯」之一。

examples.en: The supervisor explained the team norms to the students starting that week.
examples.zh: 主管给那周刚入职的学生讲了「团队共同遵守的习惯」。

words.enDefinition: an agreement among team members about practical rules for how they will work together

examples.en: Our working agreement says to mark urgent requests clearly in the team inbox.
examples.zh: 我们的「协作约定」要求在团队共用收件箱里明确标出紧急请求。

examples.en: I suggested updating the working agreement after we changed our meeting schedule.
examples.zh: 变更开会时间后，我建议更新「协作约定」。

words.enDefinition: people's preferred ways and times for sending or receiving work messages

examples.en: I checked everyone's communication preferences before sharing the handover notes with the team.
examples.zh: 把交接记录发给团队前，我先核实了每个人的「沟通方式偏好」。

examples.en: Our new supervisor asked us about communication preferences at the first team meeting.
examples.zh: 新主管在第一次团队会议上问了我们的「沟通方式偏好」。

words.enDefinition: to change the shared display of tasks to show their current status

examples.en: I had to update the task board after finishing the afternoon bookings.
examples.zh: 办完下午的预约后，我得「更新任务看板」。

examples.en: The coordinator asked me to update the task board before we started the meeting.
examples.zh: 协调员让我在开会之前「更新任务看板」。

collocations: update the task board after a meeting
remember to update the task board

words.enDefinition: to change a task's recorded status to show that its work is finished

examples.en: I waited for the supervisor's approval before I could mark a task as complete.
examples.zh: 我等主管批准后，才可以「把任务标为已完成」。

examples.en: The handbook shows where to mark a task as complete in the portal.
examples.zh: 手册指明了在平台上哪里可以「把任务标为已完成」。

collocations: mark a task as complete in the portal
be ready to mark a task as complete
click to mark a task as complete

words.enDefinition: a set of related tasks that forms one part of a larger effort

examples.en: Our workstream handled visitor information while another group prepared the display cases.
examples.zh: 我们负责的「一组相关工作任务」围绕访客信息，另一个小组负责布置展柜。

examples.en: I asked which workstream owned the rollout of the new room guides.
examples.zh: 我问新版场地指南的推出归哪「一组相关工作任务」负责。

words.enDefinition: a question that has been raised but still needs an answer or decision

examples.en: Whether the desk should open on Sundays remained an open question after the meeting.
examples.zh: 柜台周日要不要开放，开完会仍是一个「尚待明确的问题」。

examples.en: I added an open question to the notes so we could return to it.
examples.zh: 我把一个「尚待明确的问题」记到会议记录里，方便之后再讨论。

words.enDefinition: to share an unfinished version with a group so they can read or comment on it

examples.en: I offered to send around a draft before we finalized the visitor guide.
examples.zh: 访客指南定稿前，我主动提出「把草稿发给大家看」。

examples.en: The team lead will send around a draft of the new shift notes tomorrow.
examples.zh: 团队负责人明天会「把草稿发给大家看」，内容是新版的交班记录。

collocations: send around a draft for comments
offer to send around a draft
send around a draft before the meeting

words.enDefinition: to request another person's assessment before relying on a decision or answer

examples.en: I decided to ask for a second opinion before changing the event schedule.
examples.zh: 改活动安排前，我决定先「征求另一人的意见」。

examples.en: The supervisor said it was fine to ask for a second opinion about the figures.
examples.zh: 主管说，关于这些数字，可以「征求另一人的意见」。

collocations: ask for a second opinion on a draft
decide to ask for a second opinion
encourage someone to ask for a second opinion

words.zhGloss: 把这个问题留待会后谈
words.enDefinition: to move the current topic out of a meeting or group conversation for separate discussion
acceptedZhAnswers: 把这个问题留待会后谈

examples.en: I suggested we take this offline because the room booking issue needed more time.
examples.zh: 场地预约问题需要更多时间，我建议「把这个问题留待会后谈」。

examples.en: The chair said we could take this offline and focus on today's agenda.
examples.zh: 主持人说，可以「把这个问题留待会后谈」，先专注今天的议程。

collocations: suggest that we take this offline

words.enDefinition: to disagree or object in a way that remains respectful

examples.en: I had to push back politely when the new deadline overlapped with my shift.
examples.zh: 新的截止时间和我的班次冲突，我只好「礼貌地提出异议」。

examples.en: The adviser showed us how to push back politely when a request seemed unrealistic.
examples.zh: 顾问示范了请求不太现实的时候，怎样「礼貌地提出异议」。

collocations: push back politely on a deadline
feel able to push back politely

words.enDefinition: to make it clear which tasks should be handled first or given most attention

examples.en: I asked the coordinator to clarify priorities before assigning tasks to volunteers.
examples.zh: 给志愿者分任务之前，我请协调员「明确优先顺序」。

examples.en: We used the meeting to clarify priorities after the delivery date moved.
examples.zh: 交付日期调整后，我们通过开会「明确优先顺序」。

words.enDefinition: to alert the relevant people that work or delivery might be late

examples.en: I emailed the team to flag a possible delay with the printed guides.
examples.zh: 我给团队发邮件「提前提示可能延误」，说明印刷的指南可能迟到。

examples.en: The supervisor asked us to flag a possible delay as soon as we noticed it.
examples.zh: 主管让我们一发现可能来不及，就「提前提示可能延误」。

collocations: flag a possible delay to the team
use the status report to flag a possible delay
